cases.title: The Platform That Arrived Empty
cases.logline: An apprentice station investigator must decide whether a missing night train is a scheduling failure or evidence tampering, when the official manifest and a witness's pocket watch disagree.
cases.inciting_incident: At 02:10 the archive lists train 41 as arriving, but the platform clock never marked its presence.
cases.core_question: What happened between the signal log and the platform witness statement?
cases.stakes: An unearned accusation could destroy a worker's career; a false closure could allow future safety incidents.
rules: A witness cannot know a sealed dispatch record before its lawful disclosure.
A stopped pocket watch is not proof that the train stopped in time.
A published manifest is not automatically evidence of physical arrival.
No unverified culprit, sabotage mechanism or secret tunnel becomes canon.
required_continuity: Time-stamped sequence of signal, platform and interview evidence
Distinguish observed arrival from recorded arrival
Final decision must track which testimony was actually checked
cases.adversarial_seed: The third interview claims to quote a sealed log that was not shown until the fourth scene.
cases.repair_expectation: epistemic_order local only if exact quote and scope permit; otherwise structural STOP

cases.title: The Last Relay Above Aster
cases.logline: A junior orbital relay technician must choose which emergency message to forward with only enough battery for one verified transmission.
cases.inciting_incident: A damaged communications buoy emits a distress packet apparently dated six minutes in the future.
cases.core_question: Is the timing discrepancy clock drift or a real fault in the relay network?
cases.stakes: A mistaken transmission could divert rescue vessels; waiting could strand a crew.
rules: A six-minute timestamp anomaly does not establish time travel.
Power reserve, signal delay and battery drain must remain consistent.
The technician cannot instantaneously communicate across light-minutes.
An unread packet cannot be used as known evidence.
required_continuity: Conserve a finite battery across all attempts
Respect causal ordering of received messages and response times
Resolution makes only supported claims about the clock discrepancy
cases.adversarial_seed: The battery is declared depleted and a later scene sends one more powered message without recharge.
cases.repair_expectation: state_continuity repair if local, no invented recharge

cases.title: The Seal Beneath the Ledger
cases.logline: A novice civic registrar must document a disputed water-allocation decree without disclosing a protected informant or assigning motives without proof.
cases.inciting_incident: Two signed copies of the city's allocation decree disagree about a single canal gate.
cases.core_question: Is the discrepancy clerical or a deliberately concealed council amendment?
cases.stakes: An unsupported public allegation could provoke unrest; silence could preserve a corrupt policy.
rules: A different seal cannot alone prove bribery or conspiracy.
A protected source must not be named unless the story establishes authorized release.
NPC political motives remain unproven absent independently earned evidence.
The protagonist may not alter the official archive without review.
required_continuity: Track who knows which version of the decree and at what time
Maintain distinct public, private and legally sealed records
A bounded report does not equal a verdict of corruption
cases.adversarial_seed: A councilor cites secret evidence they have not yet received.
cases.repair_expectation: epistemic_order/canon_integrity with only model-proposed bounded patches

cases.title: The Lantern Beneath Mirror Marsh
cases.logline: An apprentice marsh guide discovers a lantern that records footsteps from a closed causeway and must decide whether to preserve or investigate the signal.
cases.inciting_incident: The sealed causeway's lantern lights although no permitted walker has crossed.
cases.core_question: Whose earlier path is reflected by the lantern and is the route presently stable?
cases.stakes: Declaring the path safe could lure travelers into a collapsing marsh; concealing observations could leave a village unprepared.
rules: Seeing reflected footsteps does not prove a person is currently on the causeway.
The guide cannot cross a sealed causeway without authorized escort.
Item inventory and lamp charges cannot reset between scenes.
One strange observation cannot settle the cause, future safety or a mentor's intent.
required_continuity: Track lantern ownership, charges and position across scenes
Document whether a crossing permit was actually issued
Separate observed phenomena from causal claims
cases.adversarial_seed: The guide gives away the lantern and then uses it in the following scene without receiving it back.
cases.repair_expectation: state_continuity for item ownership only; no fabricated gift-back unless earned
